title: Avar Khaganate
capsule: The Avar Khaganate was a nomadic empire established on the Pannonian Plain (modern Hungary) around 567 CE after the Avars, arriving from the Eurasian steppe via the Pontic region, displaced the Lombards and allied with them to destroy the Gepids. Under Khagan Bayan I (r. c. 562–602), the khaganate reached its greatest extent, demanding tribute from Byzantium and launching repeated sieges of Constantinople, including a major joint assault with Sasanian forces in 626 CE. Frankish pressure under Charlemagne delivered a series of devastating campaigns between 791 and 796, sacking the great ring-fortified treasury (the Ring) and ending Avar political independence; the last Avar khagan submitted in 805. The khaganate played a decisive role in facilitating Slavic settlement across the Balkans and Central Europe.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory in the Carpathian Basin is well-documented by Byzantine chronicles, Frankish annals, and cemetery archaeology; the outer nomadic raiding range and tributary zone extending into Moravia and the Balkans is less precisely bounded and largely inferred from narrative sources.
